title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
title_zh: RATED：基于执行动态的可靠性感知智能体工具检索方法

paragraphs.en: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED ( R eliability- A ware T ool retrieval via E xecution D ynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent , a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query–tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent .

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in natural language processing but are inherently unable to execute real-world actions ( Li et al., 2025 ; Naveed et al., 2025 ) . To overcome this limitation, recent systems integrate LLMs with external tools and APIs ( Mialon et al., 2023 ; Schick et al., 2023 ) , yielding autonomous AI agents that fulfill actionable requests, such as querying live databases or managing enterprise workflows ( Dong et al., 2024 ) . The fundamental bottleneck for these systems has shifted from text generation to accurately identifying and retrieving the correct entry from vast, growing tool repositories ( Patil et al., 2023 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）在自然语言处理方面展现了令人印象深刻的能力，但本质上无法执行现实世界中的操作（Li 等人，2025；Naveed 等人，2025）。 为了克服这一局限性，近期的系统将 LLM 与外部工具和 API 相集成（Mialon 等人，2023；Schick 等人，2023），从而产生了能够完成可执行请求的自主人工智能智能体，例如查询实时数据库或管理企业工作流程（Dong 等人，2024）。 这些系统的基本瓶颈已从文本生成转变为从庞大且不断增长的工具体库中准确识别和检索正确的条目（Patil 等人，2023）。

paragraphs.en: To address the tool retrieval challenge, existing research has focused on optimizing semantic relevance for Large Language Models (LLMs). Foundational works like ToolLLM ( Qin et al., 2023 ) and ToolExpNet ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) treat tool retrieval as a static ranking task. They use dense retrieval or experience networks to map queries to tool documentation based entirely on semantic relevance. While approaches such as TRFeedback ( Xu et al., 2024 ) and ToolRL ( Qian et al., 2025 ) incorporate execution feedback, they still aim to optimize how the LLM plans and invokes tools in a static environment. However, real AI agent tool ecosystems are far from static and highly unreliable. We crawl tool catalogs from LangChain ( LangChain AI, 2023 ) , CrewAI ( CrewAI, 2024 ) , LlamaIndex ( LlamaIndex, 2024 ) , and n8n ( n8n, 2024 ) to reveal the severity of this issue. As Figure 1 shows, despite rapid growth, over 50% of these tools exhibit critical flaws like broken links and missing authentication. Many tools are functionally similar, so retrieval cannot rely on semantics alone to identify which ones will execute successfully. To overcome this challenge, the system must adapt dynamically during execution. When a tool fails at runtime, the system must promptly adjust candidate ordering between requests. ToolRL cannot achieve this prompt adjustment because it uses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) to update the LLM from batched trajectories and still targets the planner. Contextual bandits ( Li et al., 2010 ) effectively address this problem. They condition each decision on the current query and update from each individual execution outcome. Moreover, they observe feedback only for the selected tool and make immediate adjustments without retraining the semantic retriever.
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决工具检索难题，现有研究主要集中在优化大语言模型（LLM）的语义相关性上。 像 ToolLLM（Qin 等人，2023）和 ToolExpNet（Zhang 等人，2025）这样的基础工作将工具检索视为一个静态的排序任务。 它们使用密集检索或经验网络，完全基于语义相关性将查询映射到工具文档上。 尽管像 TRFeedback（Xu 等人，2024）和 ToolRL（Qian 等人，2025）这样的方法纳入了执行反馈，但它们仍然旨在优化 LLM 在静态环境中规划和调用工具的方式。 然而，真实的 AI 智能体工具生态系统远非静态，而且极不可靠。 我们从 LangChain（LangChain AI，2023）、CrewAI（CrewAI，2024）、LlamaIndex（LlamaIndex，2024）和 n8n（n8n，2024）中爬取工具目录，以揭示这一问题的严重性。 如图 1 所示，尽管这些工具数量迅速增长，但超过 50% 的工具存在严重缺陷，例如失效链接和认证信息缺失。 许多工具在功能上相似，因此仅凭语义无法确定哪些工具能够成功执行。 为了克服这一挑战，系统必须在执行过程中动态适应。 当某个工具在运行时失败时，系统必须立即调整不同请求之间的候选工具排序。 ToolRL 无法实现这种提示调整，因为它使用群体相对策略优化（GRPO）（Shao 等人，2024）从批量轨迹中更新 LLM，并且仍然以规划器为目标。 上下文老虎机（Li 等人，2010）能有效解决这一问题。 它们根据当前查询对每个决策进行条件判断，并从每次单独的执行结果中进行更新。 此外，它们仅针对所选工具观察反馈，并立即进行调整，而无需重新训练语义检索器。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we propose RATED ( R eliability- A ware T ool retrieval via E xecution D ynamics), a retrieval framework that dynamically adapts to runtime tool failures without human intervention. First, we introduce EcoAgent , a benchmark of 5,172 real-world agent tools and over 210,000 query–tool pairs. Second, RATED employs a dual-encoder fine-tuned with a contrastive objective for semantic matching, together with a lightweight contextual bandit that re-ranks the top- K K candidates using a prior based on metadata and execution feedback, enabling the system to avoid failing tools. Experiments show that RATED alone keeps fault selection below 3% and recovers at both failure rates. Under a 30% failure injection protocol, RATED reduces fault selection rate to 2.9%, compared with 86.2% for the ToolLLM API retriever, while adding only 0.172 ms latency per step over encode-only inference.

paragraphs.en: We construct EcoAgent, a benchmark comprising two complementary datasets. EcoAgent complements existing tool-use datasets with metadata reliability scores for every tool and with an evaluation protocol for injected execution failures. EcoAgent-Syn supports robust training with synthetic pairs, and EcoAgent-Real supports rigorous evaluation using real-world queries. We aggregate 5,172 real-world tool definitions from four open-source AI agent platforms, namely LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, and n8n. Metadata are normalized into a shared schema with functional descriptions, names, endpoints, and authentication fields, which supports retrieval text construction and reliability scoring. To operationalize tool quality, each tool receives an automated metadata reliability score between 0 and 1 from three weighted signals, namely name–description consistency, source credibility, and documentation quality, which Section 3.3 defines. The benchmark does not rely on manual per-tool ratings. Tools with scores of at least 0.8 are marked as reliable, identifying 2,940 tools, or 56.8% of the repository. The encoder is trained only on EcoAgent-Syn, while retrieval and dynamic experiment results are validated on the EcoAgent-Real test split, with hyperparameters selected on the validation split.
paragraphs.zh: 我们构建了 EcoAgent，这是一个包含两个互补数据集的基准测试。 EcoAgent 通过为每个工具添加元数据可靠性评分，以及引入注入的执行失败评估协议，对现有的工具使用数据集进行了补充。 EcoAgent-Syn 利用合成数据对支持稳健的训练，而 EcoAgent-Real 则使用真实世界的查询支持严格的评估。 我们从四个开源 AI 智能体平台（即 LangChain、CrewAI、LlamaIndex 和 n8n）中汇总了 5,172 个真实世界的工具定义。 元数据被规范化到一个共享模式，包含功能描述、名称、端点和认证字段，这有助于检索文本构建和可靠性评分。 为了将工具质量具体化，每个工具都会根据三个加权信号（即名称与描述的一致性、来源可信度和文档质量）获得一个介于 0 到 1 之间的自动化元数据可靠性评分，这些信号在第 3.3 节中进行了定义。 该基准测试不依赖对每个工具的手动评分。 评分至少为 0.8 的工具被标记为可靠，共识别出 2,940 个工具，占整个存储库的 56.8%。 编码器仅在 EcoAgent-Syn 上进行训练，而检索和动态实验结果则在 EcoAgent-Real 测试集上验证，超参数则在验证集上选择。

paragraphs.en: We build EcoAgent-Syn with Gemma-3-1b ( Gemini Team, 2025 ) . For each tool, the model receives the tool name, functional description, and metadata as context and generates 10–20 task-oriented queries. Queries are restricted to 5–120 words, and near-duplicates with Jaccard similarity above 0.7 are removed to preserve intent diversity. Figure 2 shows the prompt template, which we also release with the dataset. To improve robustness against spurious correlations, each query is paired with hard negatives from SBERT ( Reimers and Gurevych, 2019 ) retrieval and random negatives. EcoAgent-Syn links 69,501 unique synthetic queries to 5,172 ground-truth tools, with 70,122 positive pairs and 140,244 negative pairs. For evaluation under realistic language distributions, we build EcoAgent-Real from ToolBench ( Qin et al., 2023 ) . Because the original dataset lacks ground-truth mappings to our tool repository, we implement a semi-automated labeling pipeline. GTE-Large ( Li et al., 2023 ) retrieves the top-5 candidates per query, discards pairs with cosine similarity below 0.7, and Gemma-3-1b verifies the remainder, retaining only pairs with functional match scores of at least 0.85. Human experts review a stratified sample of 200 queries and agree with the LLM verifier on 94% of cases. After filtering and deduplication, EcoAgent-Real contains 6,379 unique queries and 9,946 verified query–tool pairs.

paragraphs.en: We formulate agent tool retrieval as sequential decision making over a shared repository. Let 𝒰 = { a 1 , … , a M } \mathcal{U}=\{a_{1},\dots,a_{M}\} denote the tool pool, where M = 5,172 M{=}5{,}172 in EcoAgent. At step t t , the agent issues query q t q_{t} . The retriever returns a candidate set 𝒜 t ⊂ 𝒰 \mathcal{A}_{t}\subset\mathcal{U} with | 𝒜 t | = K |\mathcal{A}_{t}|=K , and the policy selects one tool a t ∈ 𝒜 t a_{t}\in\mathcal{A}_{t} for execution. The objective is to maximize the probability of successful execution. Unlike static retrieval with a fixed mapping f ⁡ ( q , a ) → { 0 , 1 } f(q,a)\rightarrow\{0,1\} , production agents must cope with tools that fail at runtime, where tool utility depends on semantic relevance S sem ​ ( q t , a ) S_{\text{sem}}(q_{t},a) and time-varying reliability. After execution, only the chosen tool yields binary feedback y t ∈ { 0 , 1 } y_{t}\in\{0,1\} , yielding partial feedback that we address with contextual bandits ( Abe et al., 2003 ) . Figure 3 summarizes the RATED pipeline.

paragraphs.en: At runtime, the system must adapt to dynamic failures such as API outages. Standard LinUCB ( Li et al., 2010 ) weights all past observations equally and therefore adapts slowly when arm quality shifts over time. Alternatively, a global multi-armed bandit (Global MAB) ( Auer et al., 2002 ) tracks shared or context-free arm statistics. It is cheaper to maintain but cannot model payoffs that depend on the current query context. To overcome these limitations, RATED adopts discounted LinUCB ( Garivier and Moulines, 2011 ) with a separate linear model per tool. This choice addresses non-stationarity by down-weighting older rewards before each update, ensuring that recent failures change tool scores more quickly. Each tool a a maintains 𝐀 a ∈ ℝ d × d \mathbf{A}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d} and 𝐛 a ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{b}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} . The reliability score combines exploitation and exploration.
paragraphs.zh: 在运行时，系统必须适应动态故障，例如 API 中断。 标准的 LinUCB（Li et al., 2010）对所有历史观察给予同等权重，因此当臂的质量随时间变化时，其适应能力较慢。 另一种方法是使用全局多臂老虎机（Global MAB）（Auer et al., 2002），它跟踪共享的或无上下文依赖的臂统计数据。 这种方法维护成本较低，但无法建模依赖于当前查询上下文的收益。 为克服这些局限性，RATED 采用了折扣 LinUCB（Garivier and Moulines, 2011），并为每个工具配备独立的线性模型。 这一选择在每次更新前降低旧奖励的权重，从而应对非平稳性，确保近期的故障能更快地改变工具得分。 每个工具 a 维护 𝐀 a ∈ ℝ d × d \mathbf{A}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d} 和 𝐛 a ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{b}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}。 可靠性得分结合了利用与探索。

paragraphs.en: Table 1 reports offline retrieval on EcoAgent-Syn and the held-out EcoAgent-Real test split. paragraphs.en: Table 2 reports Post-Fail SR, FSR, and adaptation steps under 20% and 30% failure injection. Static retrievers, including ToolLLM and Ada-002, frequently select unavailable tools and never recover within the evaluation horizon. DRAGON (pretrained) and BGE-Reranker reduce FSR but remain unable to adapt online. Relative to RATED (w/o Feedback), RATED (Full) lowers FSR to 2.5% and 2.9% while it maintains Post-Fail SR above 82%, which is a 7.3 × 7.3\times reduction over DRAGON (pretrained) and a 30 × 30\times reduction over ToolLLM. paragraphs.en: We profile end-to-end inference at batch size 1 on the same hardware as Section 4 . Table 3 reports average latency, P95 latency, and incremental overhead relative to DRAGON encoding only. The encode-only baseline averages 3.223 ms. RATED (w/o Feedback) applies only the static reliability prior in Eq. 5 and adds 0.025 ms. Contextual bandit re-ranking incurs modest additional cost. RATED (w/ Global MAB) adds 0.108 ms, and RATED (Full) adds 0.172 ms, reaching 3.395 ms average and 4.391 ms P95 latency. These overheads are far below batch GRPO updates similar to ToolRL at 17.839 ms average, which require periodic policy synchronization. Therefore, RATED is fast enough for interactive agent loops and still reduces fault selection.

sents.en: Contextual bandit re-ranking incurs modest additional cost.

sents.en: RATED (w/ Global MAB) adds 0.108 ms, and RATED (Full) adds 0.172 ms, reaching 3.395 ms average and 4.391 ms P95 latency.

sents.en: These overheads are far below batch GRPO updates similar to ToolRL at 17.839 ms average, which require periodic policy synchronization.
sents.zh: 这些开销远低于批量 GRPO 更新，与 ToolRL 的平均 17.839 毫秒类似，后者需要周期性的策略同步。

sents.en: Therefore, RATED is fast enough for interactive agent loops and still reduces fault selection.
sents.zh: 因此，RATED 的速度足以支持交互式智能体循环，同时仍能减少故障选择。

paragraphs.en: We introduced RATED, a reliability-aware tool retrieval framework that combines DRAGON encoders fine-tuned with contrastive learning and contextual bandit re-ranking from execution feedback. On EcoAgent, RATED achieves strong in-domain retrieval and remains competitive on real-world queries. Under injected tool failures, it reduces fault selection to 2.5–2.9% FSR, 7.3 × 7.3\times lower than static DRAGON, with only 0.172 ms added latency over encode-only inference. These results highlight the critical importance of incorporating execution feedback into retrieval systems for autonomous agents operating in dynamic environments, and demonstrate that RATED provides an efficient solution for reliable tool discovery in agent systems. Evaluating this cold-start path on newly added tools and validating RATED in live agent runtimes remain future work.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 RATED，一个具备可靠性感知能力的工具检索框架，它将通过对比学习微调的 DRAGON 编码器和基于执行反馈的上下文多臂老虎机重排序相结合。 在 EcoAgent 上，RATED 实现了强大的领域内检索能力，并在真实世界查询中保持竞争力。 在引入工具故障的情况下，其故障选择率降至 2.5–2.9% FSR，比静态 DRAGON 低 7.3 × 7.3\times，且相比仅执行编码的推理过程，额外延迟仅为 0.172 毫秒。 这些结果凸显了在执行反馈融入检索系统方面的重要性，这对在动态环境中运行的自主智能体至关重要，并表明 RATED 为智能体系统中的可靠工具发现提供了一种高效的解决方案。 在新增工具上评估这一冷启动路径，以及在实时智能体运行环境中验证 RATED，仍是未来的工作。
